Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Lumina5b elevated 5xx/timeouts — initial alert

Hi team / Alex,

We saw a spike of 5xx and backend timeouts from Lumina5b affecting a subset of requests between 08:40 and 09:05 PT this morning. Atlas reported increased failure rates from their ingestion pipeline around 08:48 — we correlated those with elevated tail latency on the rw-lumina5b model group.

Immediate notes:
- Error class: mixed 502/504 and generation timeouts (~3–4s extra on KV path).
- Affected region: us-west-2; roughly 6% of Atlas traffic (customer ID 7421).
- Mitigation in progress: temporarily routed Atlas to a lower-capacity fallback model and throttled heavy batch requests.

Ben / Marissa: can you confirm stack traces and whether any kernel-level OOMs or recent kernel rollouts coincide? Lauren — I want us to own the customer comms cadence; propose we send a short acknowledgement to Atlas within 30 minutes, followed by a recovery update and a postmortem by EOD.

Alex — apologies for the interruption. We’re actively mitigating and will follow up with more details and a timeline for the postmortem.

Thanks,
Michael

Michael / team,

Quick triage update:
- I pulled instance logs from the affected pool (rw-lumina5b-v2). No GPU OOMs. We did see increased KV cache miss rates concurrent with a small increase in concurrent prefix lengths from one heavy upstream pipeline (Atlas ingestion job).
- Kernel telemetry shows a recent LRU eviction policy tweak deployed at 03:12 PT yesterday — looks fine in general, but the eviction thresholds on the v2 pool are causing higher cache churn under the unusual prefix patterns Atlas sent.
- I’ve rolled back the LRU tweak on one canary node and re-run a synthetic workload — latency returned to baseline. Rolling the rollback across the pool now.

Attachments: debug-logs-20270618.zip (selected traces + kernel counters)

Marissa

Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 11:03:47 -0700
Subject: Action: temporary routing + request shaping for Atlas (Lumina5b)

Alex — quick update and immediate actions we put in place to reduce customer impact: 

1) Traffic routing: We moved Atlas traffic off rw-lumina5b-v2 to rw-lumina5b-v1 (smaller but more stable kernel) at 09:02 PT. Failure rate dropped to <0.5% within 6 minutes after the switch.
2) Request shaping: We applied a 1.5x concurrency cap on bulk ingestion jobs from Atlas for the next 2 hours. This is scheduled to auto-relax at 13:30 PT unless we see recurrence.
3) Rollback: Marissa reverted the LRU eviction change on the canary pool and began a controlled rollback across the v2 pool at 09:28 PT.

Next steps we promised Atlas: a recovery note in the next hour and a postmortem summary by EOD. We’ve attached a draft customer comm template and the debug logs.

Attachments: customer-comm-template.docx, debug-logs-20270618.zip

If you want me to join the customer call at 12:00 PT, I can — otherwise Michael, can you lead the external-facing post-recovery email?

Ben

Subject: Lumina5b incident — recovery confirmation and next steps

Alex / Atlas ops,

Status update: the rollback of the LRU eviction tweak across the rw-lumina5b-v2 pool completed at 12:05 PT. We have observed normal failure rates (<0.2%) and baseline latencies for your traffic since 12:10 PT.

Summary (brief):
- Root cause (preliminary): a recent LRU eviction threshold change caused increased KV cache churn for a small number of long-prefix workloads produced by Atlas’ ingestion pipeline. Under that churn the model experienced elevated tail latency leading to 502/504 responses and timeouts.
- Impact window: 08:40–12:10 PT (partial mitigation began at 09:02 PT with routing + shaping).
- Scope: ~6% of Atlas traffic, degraded generator responses and timeouts for heavy batch requests.

What we did: routing fallback, concurrency shaping, rollback of the LRU tweak, and targeted kernel telemetry collection.

What we’ll deliver:
- A detailed postmortem doc with timeline, traces, and long-term mitigation recommendations by EOD (link below).
- A follow-up call if helpful to walk through findings — proposed 14:30 PT today; let us know if that works.

Postmortem draft: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1XkLumina5bPostmortemDraft

Attachments: lumina5b-rca-draft.pdf

Thanks for your patience — we’ll circle back with the full writeup and any recommended config changes that will prevent recurrence.

Regards,
Michael
